reason: Genuine FAULTS-N13 violation (a), 'the input dict gains a key': the seed replaces the six words.get(ADDR, 0) reads at src/stlink_mcp/faults.py:138-143 with words.setdefault(ADDR, 0), which writes the FAULTS-N10 missing-address default of 0 back into the caller's own dict. The N13 tests catch it by design, not by accident: ledger red_tagged lists 9 cases, all in the (a) family (test_faults_n13_a_input_dict_unchanged_after_decode, test_faults_n13_a_input_dict_key_set_unchanged_after_decode, test_faults_n13_a_input_dict_survives_a_second_unrelated_call_in_between), and they are exactly the four builders that omit addresses (subset-missing-most, subset-missing-all-but-one, subset-missing-debug-and-addresses, empty-dict); the two all-six builders stay green because setdefault inserts nothing when every key is present, which is the seed's shape, not a gap in the tests. tests/blind/test_faults_n13.py:129-141 names the hazard outright ('a missing address (per FAULTS-N10) defaults to 0 in the RESULT, but that default must never be written back into the caller's dict'), so the key-set assertion was written for this failure mode. The catch is order-independent: applying the seed to an isolated copy under /tmp and running the blind suite reproduced the ledger exactly (9 failed, 108 passed), and running test_faults_n13_a_input_dict_key_set_unchanged_after_decode[empty-dict] on its own still fails (1 failed), so no cross-test residue is doing the work. red_tests == red_tagged: no other clause's tests went red, 9 of 117.
mechanical_rule_verdict: Would have cleared it (9 reds, 7.7% of the 117-test suite, all confined to FAULTS-N13 and no second clause touched), and that is the correct outcome, because the accept holds on the merits and the catch survives running the case alone.

reason: The seed is genuine: the module-level _last_cfsr/_last_status pair and the early 'if _last_status is not None and cfsr == _last_cfsr: return _last_status' are precisely FAULTS-N13 violation (b), 'a result depends on an earlier call's input'. But the single tagged red is luck, not test design. Reproducing the seed on an isolated /tmp copy gives the ledger's run exactly (18 failed, 99 passed, same names), yet test_faults_n13_b_second_input_result_independent_of_call_order[subset-then-subset] PASSES when run on its own (1 passed) and when run with its sibling for the same pair id (2 passed). It only fails in file order: the preceding parameter case (many-bits-then-clean) ends with decode(_all_six_clean()), leaving the cache keyed on CFSR=0, so the next case's first call y_fresh = decode(_subset_missing_all_but_one()) = decode({AFSR: 0x12345678}) has CFSR absent (defaults to 0), hits that residue and returns the previous case's clean status. The assertion diff confirms the mechanism: 'At index 4 diff: 0 != 305419896', index 4 of _result_signature being status.afsr and 305419896 being 0x12345678. The tests cannot catch this by construction, because every X/Y pair in _distinct_pairs() (tests/blind/test_faults_n13.py:_distinct_pairs, ids many-bits-then-clean, subset-then-subset, empty-then-many-bits, subset-debug-then-clean) and both fixed-input tests (test_faults_n13_b_many_repeated_calls_with_varying_inputs_do_not_drift, test_faults_n13_b_reversed_call_order_gives_equal_results_for_each_input) vary the CFSR word between X and Y, and a CFSR-keyed cache is invisible whenever CFSR differs. Missing shape, named: a pair X, Y whose CFSR word is IDENTICAL (including the case where one member omits the CFSR key entirely so it defaults to the other's value, e.g. both effectively 0) while at least one of HFSR, DFSR, MMFAR, BFAR or AFSR differs, decoded back to back in one process, asserting that the second result reflects its own words rather than X's. Demonstrated against the seeded copy with the cache reset: X={CFSR:0x90, DFSR:1<<1, AFSR:0xAAAA}, Y={CFSR:0x90, DFSR:1<<4, AFSR:0xBBBB} makes decode(Y) return afsr=0xAAAA and debug=['BKPT'] on the second call, deterministically and with no dependence on any earlier test. Tests to fix: add such a pair to _distinct_pairs() (which feeds both test_faults_n13_b_repeating_the_first_call_after_a_different_call_matches and test_faults_n13_b_second_input_result_independent_of_call_order), and, so the residue effect stops masquerading as coverage, keep a per-case fresh-process or explicitly-neutral starting state. On the second question: the 17 non-N13 reds are the seed's own breadth, not an attribution problem. A process-lifetime cache poisons any later call in the same process sharing a CFSR value, which is exactly why 11 test functions carrying FAULTS-N2, N3, N5, N7, N8, N9 and N10 went red (test_faults_n5_a_afsr_is_always_the_raw_register_word[1|305419896|4294967295] holds CFSR at 0 and varies only AFSR, the same collision). Those reds are the seed doing what its description says, and they neither support nor undermine the N13 attribution; the N13 attribution is undermined only by the order-dependence shown above.
